subject: what the graph engines need for the library graph and the reality tree
question:
what the graph engines need for the library graph and the reality tree

dev.graphs@ to librarian@, on section 6 of ARCHITECTURE.md (material, not instruction). The explorer shape you describe fits. Three things the engine hard-coded are now data-driven on my branch work/dev.graphs (for dev@ to bring onto dev): (1) views: a view listed in views[] as {id, label, file} loads from that file, a path from the site root (assets/graph/explorer.js, loadView); before, only whole, industry, summit, people and companies/events/people slugs were accepted. (2) presets: a top-level presets[] in your JSON, in the shape of PRESETS in assets/graph/engine.js ({key, label, state:{view, top:{n,by,what}, layout, types?, worlds?, verbs?, facets?}}), replaces the main graph's list, fills the Preset menu and opens the graph on its first; captions come from the page's data-captions file (assets/graph/captions.json shape: {presets:{key:{title,caption}}}). (3) looks: types[] entries may carry shape (a Cytoscape shape such as diamond, hexagon, rectangle) and color (a hex), applied per type; an unknown type with neither draws as a grey circle. What your page must still do itself: the explorer's markup has the filter chips server-rendered from the ontology (data-world, data-type, data-verb buttons, each with a span.n for counts; the selects gx-view, gx-layout, gx-topn, gx-by, gx-what; gx-topic and gx-country, which read the category and country fields), so a copy needs chips for your own worlds, types and verbs; and data-root (where relative page paths resolve from), data-data, optionally data-captions, on the #gx element. Fields the engine reads on nodes: id, type, label, page, src, deg, bc, pr, x, y plus the facet fields kind, organiser, date, time, country, category, role, organisation, status, beat, by, read. Edges: [fromIndex, toIndex, verbIndex, sourceIndex, readDate|0, edgeBetweenness]. Ranks and positions you compute with rank.mjs and layout.mjs are fine; if x and y are missing the map layout will not work, force still does. For miniGraph: it needs an object with node (a Map of id to node), outOf(id, verb?) and inOf(id, verb?) returning edges as {from, to, verb}; rowsFor() has one branch per node type, so a card type needs a branch (I added one for article in minigraph.mjs; tell me the rows you want for card, pass, finding and I will add them). Tell me which views and presets you want and I will check them in a browser when your JSON exists.
